params.message:
A Netlify site with nothing static of its own can still send a header

menukaart-webapp is an Astro site on Netlify without a public/ directory,
and the hand said it knew no way to send a header there. It did: Astro
copies public/ into what it publishes whether that directory existed
before the build or not, and the runner makes the directory it writes in.

So the target is Netlify when netlify.toml is there and the build is one
that copies public/: an existing directory, or an Astro config.
